passage:
A train line closed after a new high-speed route opened. The old tracks became quiet, and weeds grew between them.
Instead of removing the line, the city turned it into a walking and biking path. Old station signs were kept, and small boards told stories about each stop.
People began using the path on weekends. Children who had never taken the old train learned where it once went.
The line no longer carried passengers, but it still connected places.
Reuse can be a form of memory. When old infrastructure loses its first purpose, it may still guide people through history in a new way.
